newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P says may downgrade LVMH paper.
newsitem.headline: S&P says may downgrade LVMH paper.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday that it put LVMH short-term paper under watch with negative implications after the company announced that it planned to acquire control of duty free chain DFS for 12.6 billion francs.
LVMH's short-term notes are currently rated A-1+.
S&P said the acquisition of DFS would increase the group's control over the distribution of its products, but would affect its financial situation.

"Its debt would increase significantly because its pro forma net financial debt would rise to around 16 billion francs from around 3.1 billion francs on June 30, 1996," it said in a statement. LVMH's cashflow last year was 5.9 billion francs.
"Thus the flexibility that LVMH had, reflecting its low debt that was comfortably covered by cashflow, risks being reduced," it said.
S&P said it was meeting soon with LVMH managers to assess the operational impact and the company's financial objectives.
